title: Two coverings of an object have a common refinement
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and let $\mathcal U=\{U_i\to U\}_{i\in I}$ and $\mathcal V=\{V_j\to U\}_{j\in J}$ be coverings of the same object $U$. Then $\mathcal W=\{V_j\times_UU_i\to U\}_{(i,j)\in I\times J}$ (any choice of the fibre products, which exist by axiom (iii)) is a covering of $U$, and the projections $V_j\times_UU_i\to U_i$, $V_j\times_UU_i\to V_j$ with the index maps $(i,j)\mapsto i$, $(i,j)\mapsto j$ are morphisms of coverings $\mathcal W\to\mathcal U$ and $\mathcal W\to\mathcal V$ over $\mathrm{id}_U$ [def-weil-pbc-site-plus-construction] (b). In particular any finitely many coverings of $U$ have a common refinement.

mathlib_searches.query: two coverings of the same object in a site have a common refinement which is again a covering
mathlib_searches.verdict: generalization in another formalism: for covering sieves the common refinement is the intersection `intersection_covering`; for families of coverings of a Stacks site (with global pullbacks only along coverings) there is no statement; not a one-line specialization

mathlib_searches.results: only tactic uses of `refine` and the docstring 'stable under pullback and refinement' (Precoverage.lean:25); no lemma on common refinements of presieve families
